title: Invariance of a lattice pair under coefficient isomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $a:R\to S$ and $a^{\prime}:R^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ be morphisms of commutative ring sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Suppose isomorphisms $e_R:R^{\prime}\cong R$ and $e_S:S^{\prime}\cong S$ satisfy $e_S a^{\prime}=a e_R$. Let $L$ be an $S$-module sheaf and $L^{\prime}$ an $S^{\prime}$-module sheaf identified with the restriction of scalars of $L$ along $e_S$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any object $U$ of the site and any given integral lattice pair for $a^{\prime},L^{\prime}$ over $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant], there is an integral lattice pair for $a,L$ over $U$, with scalar extension interpreted as the sheafified tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: Restrict the coefficient square to the slice at U and the integral module along the inverse integral coefficient isomorphism. Apply finiteLocallyFree_restrict from LisseLatticeCoefficientNormalization to transport its finite local free generators along this equivalence of module-sheaf categories.

On sections send s tensor m to eS.inv(s) tensor m. The coefficient square proves the balancing relation; the map induced by eS.hom is inverse. Check naturality on pure tensors. Restriction of scalars along an isomorphism commutes with sheafification by its universal property, so this gives an isomorphism of the scalar extensions.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), rationalization of a lattice pair

proof.text: Compose this isomorphism with the given pair rationalization and the slice restriction of the module identification. The double coefficient restrictions cancel, giving a rationalization to L restricted at U.
